description:
You are a quantitative developer at Atlas Capital Management. The risk team has scaffolded a PortfolioAnalytics library with interface contracts for three core risk metrics, but the implementations are empty stubs that return 0. The head of risk has given you a week of historical return data (250 trading days) for a 3-asset portfolio and needs the engine to be production-ready by end of day.

Open the PortfolioAnalytics solution in Visual Studio 2022 and implement the three risk metric classes:

1. VaRCalculator: Implement Historical Simulation Value-at-Risk at the 95% confidence level. Given a List<double> of daily P&L returns, return the loss (positive number) at the 5th percentile — i.e., sort ascending and take the value at index floor(n * 0.05), then negate it to express as a positive loss.

2. SharpeRatioCalculator: Implement the annualized Sharpe Ratio. Formula: (mean_daily_return - risk_free_daily_rate) / std_dev_daily_return * sqrt(252). The risk-free rate is passed as an annual decimal (e.g., 0.04 for 4%). Convert to daily: risk_free_daily = annual / 252.

3. MaxDrawdownCalculator: Implement maximum drawdown as a positive fraction (0 to 1). Running peak starts at first return. For each return, update running cumulative P&L sum; track the peak and compute drawdown = (peak - current) / peak when peak > 0. Return the maximum such drawdown seen. If no drawdown occurs, return 0.

All implementations must match the IPortfolioRiskCalculator interface exactly. The solution must build with 0 errors. Windows user: Docker, password: GymAnything123!
